original.target_description: Simple headphones-on versus headphones-off comparison of time looking at Black discussant during offensive comments.

n.sample_role: non-Black undergraduates in the eye-tracking experiment
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for this test.
n.quote: Twenty-five non-Black undergraduates participated for course credit or a payment of $10.

p.quote: roughly 5 times longer (Tukey’s p < .01) in the headphones-on condition

replication.target_description: Time spent looking at a Black man after a White man makes a potentially offensive comment in his presence, comparing whether the Black man can versus cannot hear the comment. ML5 Revised protocol; pooled replication meta-analysis.

n.sample_role: participants reported as N in the protocol column; analytic denominator and exclusions not independently documented here
n.location: p. 11, Table 3, corresponding study row, ML5 Revised protocol N column

es.location: Table 4, Crosby, J. R., Monin, B., & Richardson, D., Revised protocol

p.location: Table 4, Crosby, J. R., Monin, B., & Richardson, D., Revised protocol

reported_success.location: Discussion, Specific implications for replicability of these 10 findings
reported_success.quote: None of the replication studies for Crosby et al. achieved statistical significance on their own, but the cumulative evidence supports the original finding, albeit with a reduced effect size.

notes: Replication ES and p are paired from Table 4. Table 3 supplies protocol N; some Table 3 point estimates/intervals differ slightly from Table 4. Narrative success is not inferred from p.  The printed partial eta squared .18 and F(3,69)=5.15 concern the omnibus headphones × discussant interaction, not this simple comparison; they were not paired with the simple-comparison p.
